samples.marker: Urelas MSMP loader: remove unproven keylogging and DKOM claims
evidence: Outer 0x40203a-0x40209d opens HKCU Windows NT/CurrentVersion/Windows and writes its Run value; 0x4020b8 launches the installed image.
Outer 0x406d97/0x406e08 validates MSMP state; the 512-byte complement loop conceals the stored configuration.
Outer 0x402c80 calls the network fetch path at 0x4067a0; 0x40699d opens the received file and 0x4069be receives its body through 0x4064d0.
ZIP at file 0x38c68..0x67cdc decrypts with password 1234 to HanAgent_p.exe, sha256 a86e110dcf8d6884dd8f7c026bef797169cfd31caec5f86acfdf6c80b7fd0f39.
Emulated only the child unpacker with stubbed Win32 APIs; stopped at recovered entry 0x41382a. No native sample execution or live C2 interaction.
Unpacked child targets highlow2.exe, LASPOKER.exe, poker7.exe, Baduki.exe and related Korean game clients; 0x403370 writes a DLL path to remote memory and starts a LoadLibraryW thread at 0x403477.
Child capture routine 0x403570 calls PrintWindow at 0x40372a and extracts bitmap data. Separate socket routines call Winsock send at 0x404166/0x404173.
Outer SetWindowsHookExW at 0x412748 receives WH_CBT=5, NULL module, and GetCurrentThreadId result; it is a thread-local MFC window hook.

Former rootkit matcher requires names and diagnostics only; it does not establish a kernel-memory write or list unlink. Relocated the unchanged reference conjunction to a notable kernel-debug profile; generic memory names/formats moved to memory capability leaves.
0x401150 creates a host process, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes it to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401260 opens LanmanServer/Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL, and replaces it with the loader DLL path at 0x40133e.

Selected configuration mode is 3 at 0x404120. The entry dispatcher takes the Active Setup branch at 0x401f8a; 0x401900 creates an Installed Components GUID key, writes StubPath, patches/copies the image and starts the copy.
0x401390 obtains its own short path and COMSPEC, builds /c del ... > nul, and invokes CreateProcessA.

The resource section is entirely zero-filled; resource extraction cannot supply the original DLL in these bytes. Existing findings explicitly describe surviving code/API evidence rather than successful installation.
Storm ddos Server and Welcome to use storm ddos banners identify StormAttack. There is no evidence of WannaCry encryption in the surviving code.
PKCS7 signer cryptography verifies but the signed image digest does not match; the copied Microsoft identity establishes no authentic Microsoft program provenance.

samples.marker: myRunner association hijacker: clarify TIMP1atform lookalike
evidence: 0x4063c0 opens HKLM Software/Classes/exefile/shell/open/command. It stages its executable through 0x405440, truncates the extension at 0x406517, appends the quoted %1/%* wrapper template, then writes through registry helper 0x404610.
0x4065a8 repeats the mechanism for the txtfile handler. This is interception of ordinary executable/document launches with extension concealment, beyond normal handler registration.
0x405440 reads/writes executable contents and preserves timestamps. Live code remains in the unnamed executable section despite erased resource and .PEC sections.
Tencent QQ registry targets, TIMP1atform.exe lookalike, myRunner updater URL, Online.ie mailbox and zigui configuration references corroborate myRunner/QQpass identity.
POP3-related names and network APIs alone do not establish a working mailbox-controlled payload path in these modified bytes; no additional mail-loader verdict was added.
Corrected the lookalike descriptions to spell the actual TIMP1atform marker. No ransomware behavior was established.
